bitstream_source: main 32267ee8 by the bench's nightly job (icepi/build/v1.3.bit)
firmware_sha256: of each python/bench_firmware.py entry as sorted, compact JSON, or of the test/ file, at the run's commit
bench: an Icepi Zero (ECP5 LFE5U-25F) running the chip at 48 MHz on bench carrier v1.2, Pico A as the host on SPI, nothing, Pico B idle on OUT0, analyser A (fx2lafw) at 24 MS/s
scope: the bytes on the wire and their timing in one run of spdif_codecs, as the analyser saw them
limits: one run of one board, the ECP5 build of the chip's RTL, not the ASIC
the run's files are the bench's own record, tied together by SHA256SUMS, and CI derives the decode and the timing from the capture alone
each edge is known to a sample either way and the analyser's crystal to 100 ppm, and a window the capture cannot settle is unresolved, not passed
the bitstream is named by its sha256, and its netlist's, built from main 32267ee8 by the bench's nightly job (icepi/build/v1.3.bit) by the bench's notes, which CI does not rebuild
our own demo on the held-out S/PDIF firmware, not a drawn or sealed protocol, sending a chirp that FFmpeg encoded as AC-3, MP3, AAC and DTS and muxed to IEC 61937 bursts
sigrok's spdif misreads the bursts, so its decode is not judged
demo/ffmpeg_referee.py reads the words by run length, and FFmpeg's spdif demuxer must name each codec and find the frames sent in its bursts
FFmpeg holds the frames' bytes, not the line code
the Pico pushes each burst at its place and the firmware starts it on a frame, so a burst is held to its period within 8 words, not to IEC 61937's exact repetition
the line runs at 44.1 kHz for every codec, which no receiver was asked to lock to
a half slot is about four samples, so its windows can stay unresolved
